Senior Software Engineer - AI Evaluation / Coding Agents is a remote engineering review track for evaluating production code, debugging traces, and developer-facing AI outputs against real-world correctness standards. Reviewers reproduce failures, write the unit test the model should have written, and explain the fix so the modeling team can target the gap.

**Why this role matters**
-------------------------

Engineering model quality lives or dies on whether the generated code actually compiles, passes tests, and handles edge cases. AuraOne pairs experienced engineers with the modeling team to grade outputs the way a code reviewer would.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

* Run and reproduce candidate code outputs in a sandboxed environment for Senior Software Engineer - AI Evaluation / Coding Agents assignments.
* Grade senior software engineer ai evaluation / coding agents engineering review solutions for correctness, style, and edge-case handling.
* Write minimal failing tests that demonstrate the bug a model output missed.
* Compare paired solutions and rank them with a written rationale tied to the rubric.
* Tag failure modes (compile error, runtime crash, off-by-one, security issue) with severity scores.
* Document recurring code-generation failures so the modeling team can target them.
* Calibrate against gold-standard reviews to keep inter-rater agreement above target.

**Qualifications**
------------------

* Strong day-job engineering experience — you can read, run, and debug unfamiliar code for Senior Software Engineer - AI Evaluation / Coding Agents work.
* Comfort writing concise unit tests that capture a single failure mode.
* Familiarity with a testing framework. pytest, Jest, or JUnit. Go test, RSpec, or whatever you use.
* Clear written reasoning — your review note has to convince another senior engineer.
* Reliable async availability for at least 10 hours per week.
* Prior code-review or technical-interview-grading experience is a plus.

**Example tasks**
-----------------

* Reproduce a generated engineering solution to a coding task, run the test suite, and grade it.
* Write the smallest failing test that demonstrates a model's edge-case bug.
* Compare two paired solutions and rank them with a written rationale tied to the rubric.
* Triage a security issue surfaced by a model and document the patch the model should have produced.

**Nice to have**
----------------

* Open-source contributions or a public portfolio that demonstrates production-quality code.
* Experience with the target language's standard tooling, linters, and idiomatic style guides.
* Familiarity with security-review checklists (OWASP, CWE) and AppSec patterns.

**Passionate about precision medicine and advancing the healthcare industry?**

Recent advancements in underlying technology have finally made it possible for AI to impact clinical care in a meaningful way. Tempus' proprietary platform connects an entire ecosystem of real-world evidence to deliver real-time, actionable insights to physicians, providing critical information about the right treatments for the right patients, at the right time.

We are seeking an exceptional AI Scientist/Engineer to bridge two cutting-edge domains in medical AI: **Oncology Foundation Models** and **Agentic Systems**. In this role, you will design and train domain-specific foundation models on complex, multimodal cancer datasets (genomics, histopathology, longitudinal EHRs, and clinical imaging) while simultaneously building agentic workflows that orchestrate these models.

By integrating foundation models with agentic frameworks, you will help create intelligent clinical tools capable of dynamic reasoning, multi-step evidence synthesis, and complex decision support in oncology.

**Core Responsibilities**
-------------------------

1. Oncology Foundation Model Development

* Design, train, and fine-tune large-scale multimodal foundation models specialized in oncology (e.g., integrating spatial transcriptomics, whole-slide images, and clinical histories).
* Implement pre-training strategies tailored to bio-medical domains, including self-supervised learning (SSL), contrastive learning, and masked token prediction.
* Evaluate model robustness, generalization, and domain shift across diverse patient cohorts, tumor types, and sequencing platforms.

2. Agentic Platform Engineering

* Architect scalable agentic frameworks (e.g., tool-use, multi-agent communication, autonomous planning, and retrieval-augmented generation) tailored for clinical workflows.
* Design safety guards, reasoning trace verification, and human-in-the-loop interventions for AI agents operating in high-stakes medical settings.
* Integrate agentic systems with external biological knowledge bases, literature databases (PubMed, clinical trials), and EHR interfaces.

3. Connecting Models & Agents (The Synergy)

* Expose specialized oncology foundation models as core tools/capabilities within the agentic platform, enabling agents to dynamically invoke multi-omic analysis tools.
* Develop agent-driven workflows that use foundation models to summarize complex patient trajectories, propose biomarker-driven treatment hypotheses, or query trial eligibility.
* Optimize end-to-end latency, reasoning chains, and output interpretability for clinical and scientific research end-users.
